title: Cipher opening in Johan van Ewsum's register of land rents, Groninger Archieven 696 inv. 595 (catalogue 2533): a letter on soldiers' pay and a note on the truce with the cities of the Sticht, addressed to Hackfort and Meinert van Ham, read with the writer's own key

steps.what: Viewer opened by headless Chromium (scripts/anl_probe.py, a port of the sweep's anl_view2.js that logs image requests); the two full images (scans 193 and 1) fetched once each from the IIP server.
Sign conventions written before any value was applied; pass 1 on scan 193, pass 2 on scan 1; 4 differences settled at 3x.
Key read from the two key lines and the clear note on the same page and frozen (key_frozen.tsv) before the first decryption (by the contributor's record: one commit).

Whole text held out from the key: with the frozen key unchanged, 116 of 119 cipher words decrypt to words of the period language; the writer's repeated clause (L08-L09, L10-L11) gives the same 35 signs in both copies.

Mechanical decryption read as Low Saxon with every departure marked; scripts/check_marks.py rebuilds the decryption and passes. Dan's docs/_check_reading.py: 0.571 (reading file, language picked by the checker: fr), 0.400 (decryption), 0.714 (translation); its word lists do not cover 16th-century Low Saxon.
Two web searches; no edition or reading of this opening.

Integration check (13 Nov 2026): check_marks.py passes; own decoder from key.tsv and the transcription gives the same 33 lines; scan 1 re-fetched (2225 x 3000 px): the 22 key letters and the null note read as in key.tsv, and the first 15 words of L01-L05 (about 45 signs) agree with the transcription. Strict share first recorded as 120 of 123 words (97.6%); recounted by the claims reader on 13 Nov 2026 as 116 of 119 words (the earlier count included colons and dashes), and 116 of 123 = 94.3% with the four struck groups counted as holes. Not checked: the dating (1533-1536) and the identification of Hackfort, Meinert van Ham and Schenck, which are the contributor's inference; writer and recipients open.

outcome.method_basis: The writer's own key alphabet and null note at the head of the cipher page; the key was applied unchanged. Catalogue correction: the text is a letter and a note on soldiers' pay and a truce, not recipes.
outcome.fraction_read_source: 116 of 119 cipher words verbatim from the signs (reading.py, corrected 13 Nov 2026 to skip colons and dashes); with the 4 struck groups counted as holes, 116 of 123 = 94.3% (the contributor gave 120 of 123 = 97.6%, which counted punctuation tokens and left the struck groups out). The sweep of 11 Nov 2026 found no other cipher in the register.

texts.label: Cipher opening, scan 193: letter, note, address and formula
texts.summary: A letter to 'good friends': the soldiers' pay came yesterday with the envoys and Hendricus; send the account and receipt at once and see how to get it over safely; about twenty soldiers who were out with the colonels could be used for it, so that at Wedde on 10 July the envoy and those not covered by the payment are summoned. A note to 'Heer Drost', signed Hendricus: the truce between 'my gracious lords' and the cities of the Sticht is extended by a month, but Jorien Schenck (probably Georg Schenck van Toutenburg) will not keep it, so travel over the open country will be dangerous. Address: to Hackfort and Meinert van Ham, colonel(s). Under a rule a formula 'ergo : tergo : be[...]lo' with the clear Latin caption 'ad perforandum caput gallinae'.
texts.note: Words: 119 cipher words (not counting colons and dashes), 116 verbatim from the signs (97.5%; 94.3% of 123 with the 4 struck groups counted as holes), 1 with a marked repair (knech{+t}en), 0 guesses, 2 holes (signs under blots; a word with a blotted sign counts as a hole even where a letter is proposed for it, as in L03 ambasiate[n]). Two renderings doubtful in sense, not in the signs: 'sich verechtert hebben' and the syntax of L17-L20. Dan's reading checker scores 0.400 (decryption), 0.571 (reading, language picked fr) and 0.714 (translation) because its word lists lack 16th-century Low Saxon (nl does not know 'gecomen', 'heren', 'lant'); a human reader should judge the sentences.

reading_review.note: Five cipher lines (L01, L06, L10, L11, R04) re-copied from scan 193 agree sign for sign with the transcription; check_marks passes and the writer's own key, frozen before decryption, gave 120 of 123 words verbatim by the contributor's count (116 of 119 after the recount of 13 Nov 2026). All 7 prose sentences of the letter, the note and the address read as coherent Low Saxon against the English; the sense of 'sich verechtert hebben' and the syntax of L17-L20 remain doubtful.

gaps.item: Two blotted signs (L03 last letter of ambasiate-, R10 third sign of be[...]lo)
gaps.detail: Under ink blots on the scan; the original might show more.

gaps.item: Four struck groups (L04, L11, L17, R10)
gaps.detail: Deleted by the writer under ink; the shape under the ink was taken as a hash or knot and not read as a sign. Not part of the 119 words, but counted as holes in the strict share (116 of 123 = 94.3%).

gaps.item: Sense of 'sich verechtert hebben' (L14-L15) and of the clause L17-L20
gaps.detail: The words read; the meaning of two phrases does not settle from a text of this size. A reader of Middle Low German or Middle Dutch should check the translation.

prior.where: No reading found: catalogue vetting of 11 Nov 2026 (DECODE, cryptiana, Perton 2017, Kluyver 1900) and two web searches on 12 Nov 2026 (Ewsum with geheimschrift and the Latin caption; Meinert van Ham, Hackfort, Schenck, Ewsum). Rutgers' 1899 inventory not opened.

human: WAINUT set the task (catalogue 2533) and the rules; AI language-model agents fetched the images, transcribed, froze the key, decrypted and read. No target-specific human intervention. No human palaeographer checked the text.
